Sensor hint

Off by default. After a sensor change logged in AAPS: a note for the first 2 hours, and for a jump of 1.5 mmol/L or more in 5 minutes during the first day. Only a note: values and alarms stay as they are, the loop is not touched. Do not calibrate then; check with a finger stick.

Cannula hint
Off by default. A cannula of 60 hours or more and 40 % or more of the last 6 hours over 10 mmol/L: probably the cannula, consider a change. Only a note, nothing is changed.

Change evaluation

Off by default. A change applied with the learner\'s \"Apply\" is judged 3 days later against the 3 days before it. Worse: under 3.9 up by 1.5 points or more, or under 3.0 up by 0.5 or more. Better: fewer lows (or 3 points fewer over 10) without more lows and swings. Rollback rule: under 3.0 more than 1 % two days in a row, or a value under 2.5 -> \"check whether to undo it\". Nothing is undone by itself. Days with a cannula failure, a new sensor or illness are not left out: judge them yourself.

Meal at a low glucose

Off by default. A meal of 13 g or more logged at a glucose under 4.5: a note "fast carbs first". Such a meal often ends low anyway, with or without a bolus, because the food lifts too slowly. Only a note.

Special day
Illness, a cannula failure, a party: for 24 hours the learner makes no cards, and the readings of that time are left out of every card and verdict later. It ends by itself after 24 h.

Insulin peak check (nights)

Off by default. With the basal card: at night without food the glucose change is compared with insulin curves of peak 25-75 min (DIA as in the profile); the best fit is shown. A proposal only when it is 10 min or more away from the profile peak and fits clearly better. It changes nothing: the peak is set by the family in the insulin settings.

Low forecast

Off by default. Every 5 min: smoothed glucose + 6 x its fall per 5 min = glucose in about 30 min. Under 3.9 with the glucose under 6.5 and falling: a notice. Each notice is checked 40 min later; many false ones make it stricter, it never gets looser than at the start without many true ones. Only a notice.

Rebound guard

Off by default. After a hypo treatment (12 g or less at glucose under 4.5) for 3 hours: no SMB and the temp basal not above the profile basal. Lets go at once when a meal is logged, at glucose 13.9 or more, or early when insulin is really needed: a strong rise over 9, a rise far above what the treatment explains, or a flat high over 10 after 45 minutes. It only takes insulin away: it never gives more, never blocks your bolus. Manual temp basals in these 3 hours are capped too.

Split meal bolus

Off by default. GIVES INSULIN. Dose = carbs / CR of now, minus the bolus insulin still active. Fast meal: all now. Normal: 60 % now. Slow: 50 % now. The rest is checked every minute from 20 min: given only when the smoothed glucose is 5.5 or more and rising (0.5 in 15 min); never under 4.5 or while falling; minus all other boluses given meanwhile (SMB, a manual or SMS correction); dropped after 90 min (slow 180) with a notice. Every dose goes through the pump queue with all AAPS limits.

Profile percentage watch

Off by default. Only a notice, it changes nothing. 1) The percentage is over 100 % for 4 hours or more: a reminder, again every 4 hours. 2) The percentage came down from over 100 % less than an hour ago and the active insulin is 1.0 U or more: the insulin of the high hours still works, watch the next hour for a low. 4 h, 1 h and 1.0 U are our estimates.

Hints to Nightscout (iPhone)

Off by default. Important hints (insulin curve changed, low forecast, cannula, sensor, profile percentage, split bolus not given) are also written as an announcement, which AAPS uploads to Nightscout. So the family sees them on the iPhone. Only text: no treatment is written. The same text is not sent again within 6 hours.
Night target (lows at night)

Off by default. With the basal card, every 4 days. Last 14 days, night = 21:00 to 06:00. If a low (15 min or more under 3.9) came in 40 % of the nights or more and the night time over 10 is 10 % or less: a proposal to raise the night target by 1.0 mmol/L (never over 8.0). Only HIGHER = less insulin at night, but more highs are possible. Lab: fewer lows, a bit more highs. \"Внести\" edits the profile target for 21-06 h; it is judged in 3 days.
